column1: Feed your starter ahead of time so it is bubbly, active and doubled before you begin.
In a large bowl stir together the starter, water and olive oil with a fork, then add the flour and salt. Mix, then finish by hand until no dry flour remains. The dough will be shaggy.
Cover and rest 30 minutes to 1 hour, then work the dough into a rough ball for about 15 seconds.
Cover with lightly oiled wrap and let rise in a warm spot until almost doubled and no longer dense, about 2–4 hours in summer or 10–12 hours in winter.
Optional: starting 30–45 minutes into the rise, do 2–3 sets of stretch-and-folds about an hour apart to build strength.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and fold the edges into the center all the way around. Flip seam-side down and rotate with cupped hands to tighten into a ball.
Line a Dutch oven with parchment or dust with cornmeal, place the dough inside, cover and let rise 30 minutes to 1 hour until slightly puffy. Preheat the oven to 450°F (232°C).
Just before baking, slash the top about 1/4 inch deep and 2–3 inches long.
Put the covered pot in the oven, lower the heat to 400°F (204°C) and bake 20 minutes.
Remove the lid and bake about 40 minutes more until deep golden brown and 205–210°F (96–98°C) inside.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 1 hour before slicing.
